Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

If it's a minor issue, mediation might be feasible. In conclusion, while not solely responsible, Kwame can support reconciliation by facilitating communication and emphasizing the event's importance, always respecting each friend's feelings and boundaries.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for someone to delete their stepbrother's profile on their Nintendo Switch. Let me start by understanding the situation better. So, the person had to watch their stepbrother for a week while their dad and his mom were on a trip. They brought their Switch along because they wanted something to do during their long train commute to school. The stepbrother wanted to play on it, and it actually helped distract him while the person studied. So, to prevent the stepbrother from messing up their saves, they created a new profile for him on the Switch. When they got back to school, they got annoyed with having to switch profiles every time they started a game or went to the eShop. So, they decided to delete the stepbrother's profile. Now, during Thanksgiving, when the stepbrother tried to play, he found out his Zelda save was gone and started crying, which made the situation pretty emotional. The person's dad thinks it was mean to delete the profile because the stepbrother was enjoying playing. The person didn't think it was a big deal since they usually don't bring their Switch over when visiting. Alright, so I need to determine if deleting the profile was right or wrong. Let's break it down. First, the person created the profile to help the stepbrother and keep their own saves safe. That seems considerate. But then, after a while, they got annoyed with switching profiles and decided to delete it without telling the stepbrother. That seems a bit harsh. The stepbrother was emotionally affected, which shows that the action had a negative impact. The dad also thinks it was mean, which adds to the perception that it might not have been the best decision. On the other hand, the person felt it was their property and they had the right to manage it as they saw fit. They also mentioned that they usually don't bring the Switch over, so maybe they felt it wasn't a big deal. But considering the emotional response and the fact that the stepbrother was using it with permission, deleting the profile without discussing it first seems unfair. It's one thing to manage your own belongings, but when someone else is using it and has created content or saves, deleting it without warning can feel like a personal slight. Maybe a better approach would have been to talk to the stepbrother about their concerns and find a compromise, like keeping the profile but maybe setting some boundaries or explaining why they wanted to delete it. That way, both parties feel heard and respected. So, in conclusion, while the person had the right to manage their Switch, the way they handled it by deleting the profile without communication was probably not the best approach and could be seen as mean or unfair.
